title: A seat steady and easy
hookLine: the serpent called Endless, and a book that gives the poses one line
carry: asana is a steady, easy seat for the mind
tomorrow: sit apart from the world, or act in it: which one is yoga?

lines: MATS IN ROWS, A LONG HOLD.
cards: A yoga class in a strip mall at six in the evening: mats in rows, everyone shaking in a long hold. Now an older picture. Vishnu rests on the great serpent Adishesha, also called Ananta, the Endless.
A story many yoga schools tell says the serpent asked to be born on earth to teach, and fell as a tiny snake into the cupped hands of a woman at prayer. That was Patanjali.
And in his Yoga Sutras, the poses get one short line.

teach.b: Sutra 2.46, in paraphrase: the posture is steady and easy. Sthira, steady. Sukha, easy.
That's the whole definition. Why so little? Because in the sutras, asana means a seat, something you can stay in, not a shape to perform.
The next sutra says how it's mastered: by relaxing effort and letting the mind rest on the endless. The word there is ananta, the serpent's own name.

Some teachers hear an echo here: a seat like that coil under Vishnu, holding steady without strain. Then 2.48: from that, one is no longer struck by the pairs of opposites, heat and cold, praise and blame.
And where does posture sit in the path?
Sutra 2.29 lists eight limbs, and it's the third: after the restraints and observances, before breath, turning the senses inward, concentration, meditation and absorption.
So here's the teaching, plainly: in Hindu yoga, the body is made steady so the mind can turn inward, toward the Self.
The pose is a doorway, not the house. On its journey west, that third limb grew until it could look like all of yoga. The sutras aren't against stretching.
They keep asking what it's for.

how: In traditional settings, asana prepares a steady seat for breath practice and meditation, as Yoga Sutras 2.46–2.48 describe.

games.q: a friend wants to try yoga but says she can't: she isn't flexible. by sutra 2.46, what's the reply?
o: stretch for a month first, then try.
skip the body; yoga is only meditation.
the pose is a seat, steady and easy. flexibility isn't the test.
games.why: Patanjali's whole definition of posture is steady and easy. it's a seat you can stay in, not a shape to perform.

practice: Find a seat you could keep for a while, upright but not stiff. Adjust until it's both steady and easy, then stop adjusting. Let the effort of holding yourself up soften a little on each out-breath, and stay.
